ancestry.selection: first accepted sample with recorded midpoint contact

source.note: Printed reciprocal K/R and endpoint data are not mutually reproduced by this ideal DC law; discrepancy retained, not calibration.

assumptions: Mass, yaw/wheel/rotor inertia, tire friction and load distribution are hypotheses; no complete mass estimate exists.
Motor viscous drag is a named hypothesis using K times reported no-load current divided by reported free speed, not a measured friction curve.
Ideal rigid gearing; rotor inertia reflected once into axle inertia, no duplicate energy.
Each side has three tire contacts with prescribed normal fractions; center-drop contact and dynamic load transfer are not solved.
Regularized friction circle models longitudinal slip and lateral scrub. No magic wheel-speed-to-chassis-speed assignment.
Caller supplies bus voltage and normal loads; no hidden battery. Signed regenerative power is preserved.
Ideal phase current limit and dissipative brake mode are controller hypotheses, not selected-controller behavior.
